sources.name: SPARQL 1.1 Protocol
sources.role: HTTP/SOAP request-response bindings for SPARQL query and update operations, dataset parameters, status and transport contract
verified_facts: SPARQL 1.1 Protocol defines how SPARQL query and update operations are conveyed to a SPARQL service.
The protocol defines request parameters, dataset selection and response behavior over standard Web protocols.
Protocol success and HTTP response handling concern operation transport and service interaction.
semantic_limits: A successful protocol exchange proves request processing, not source authority, dataset completeness or physical truth.
HTTP status and returned result serialization do not establish that the underlying source object is immutable or fully received.
A returned numeric value must not create a parcel-height row without exact source bytes, cadastral polygon, CRS, vertical datum, units, method and execution receipts.

sources.name: SPARQL 1.1 Service Description
sources.role: SPARQL endpoint capability, supported language, result format, entailment regime, graph and feature-discovery contract
verified_facts: SPARQL 1.1 Service Description defines an RDF vocabulary for describing SPARQL service capabilities.
A service description can advertise supported query languages, result formats, entailment regimes and features.
The description can identify default and named graphs exposed by a service.
semantic_limits: Advertised capability is metadata about a service and does not prove that a particular request used or satisfied that capability.
A listed graph or entailment regime does not establish authoritative cadastral identity, data freshness or measurement accuracy.
Service metadata must not substitute for source-byte, geometry, CRS, vertical-datum and execution receipts.

sources.name: SPARQL 1.1 Update
sources.role: RDF graph mutation operations, graph management, dataset update sequence and atomic-operation semantics contract
verified_facts: SPARQL 1.1 Update defines operations that modify, create or remove RDF graph content.
Update requests can include INSERT, DELETE, LOAD, CLEAR, CREATE, DROP, COPY, MOVE and ADD operations.
Update execution changes the graph store state addressed by the request.
semantic_limits: A successful update confirms mutation processing, not that inserted assertions are authoritative or physically true.
Graph-store state after an update is not an immutable source snapshot unless exact before/after objects and digests are recorded.
Inserted numeric literals must not become terrain results without authoritative source, parcel geometry and measurement receipts.

sources.name: RDF 1.1 TriG
sources.role: RDF dataset textual syntax, graph labels, default/named graph blocks, prefixes, base IRI and parser contract
verified_facts: RDF 1.1 TriG defines a concrete syntax for serializing an RDF dataset.
TriG can represent a default graph and multiple named graphs in one document.
TriG uses Turtle-style terms, prefixes and base-IRI resolution inside graph blocks.
semantic_limits: Successful TriG parsing establishes syntax-to-dataset conversion, not authority, completeness or physical correctness.
Graph labels and named-graph boundaries are dataset structure and do not prove persistent cadastral parcel identity.
Equivalent RDF datasets may have different source bytes, so dataset equality cannot replace exact-object digest and measurement receipts.
